mainTopic: A seller who chases his money, the limit on charging workers who back out, and a renter who changes a donkey's route.
overview: The גמרא first finishes an answer from the previous page. A seller who keeps chasing his money may have sold because his field was poor, not because he needed cash. It calls one case obvious: a seller who was forced into a bigger sale clearly needed money. It then asks about a seller who could have found an easier sale with effort but did not bother, and that question ends in a תיקו. Next it explains the משנה about a חמר or קדר who backs out. רב נחמן limits what the employer may charge them to the wages he owes them. רבא challenges him from a ברייתא that allows up to 40 or 50 זוז, and רב נחמן answers that the ברייתא is about a case where the worker's bundle is in the employer's hands. A new משנה then rules on a renter who changes a donkey's route between mountain and valley, and on what the owner owes when the donkey becomes ill, is seized, dies or breaks a leg. The גמרא asks why the first ruling of the משנה makes no distinctions, and it gives several answers: death from the air, from exhaustion, or from a snake bite, or that the ruling follows רבי מאיר.

steps.title: The seller sold because his field was poor
steps.stepSummary: The last words of an answer from the previous page: the case where the buyer still acquires is one where the seller sold his field because it was poor quality.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The other case is talking about one who sells his field] because of its poor quality.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an answer it began on the previous page. It explains that the seller in that case sold because his field was bad, not because he desperately needed money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, a seller who keeps running after his money shows that he sold only because he needed cash. Here, though, the reason for the sale is that the field is poor, so his chasing the money does not prove that kind of need. This is the idea the next steps build on.

phrases.english: because of its poor quality.
phrases.notes: These are the last words of a sentence that started on the previous page: 'the case there is one who sells his field...'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer to a contradiction raised on the previous page.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction: the other case is a seller of a poor field.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every seller who chases his money must have sold because he needed cash.
steps.terutzMaskana: A seller of a poor-quality field chases his money for a different reason, so his case is different.

steps.title: The obvious case: the seller clearly needed money
steps.stepSummary: If he wanted to sell for 100, could not find a buyer, sold for 200, and keeps chasing the money, then obviously the buyer has not acquired.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious: if he wanted to sell [property] for 100 and did not find [a buyer], and he sold for 200, and he keeps going in and out after the money, [the buyer] has not acquired.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a case it calls obvious. This sets up the harder question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He only wanted to sell 100 worth, but nobody would buy that, so he was forced to sell 200 worth. Together with his chasing the money, this clearly shows financial pressure, so the buyer has not acquired. This is unlike the seller of the poor field.

keyTerms.meaning: goes in and out after the money (keeps chasing payment)

phrases.english: It is obvious: if he wants to sell for one hundred
and does not find [a buyer], and sells for two hundred,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָא עָיֵיל וְנָפֵיק אַזּוּזֵי – לָא קָנֵי.
phrases.english: and he goes in and goes out for the money, [the buyer] has not acquired.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the idea from step 1 to set up a clear baseline case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seller who was forced into a larger sale and chases the money clearly sold out of need, so the buyer has not acquired.

steps.title: The unclear case: he could have found a buyer but didn't try
steps.stepSummary: What if, with some effort, he could have found a buyer for 100, but he did not bother and sold for 200? Is he like the seller of a poor field or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he wanted to sell for 100 and did not find [a buyer], but if he had made an effort he would have found one, and he did not make the effort and sold for 200, and he keeps going in and out after the money, what [is the law]? Is he considered like one who sells his field because of its poor quality, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about a middle case that falls between the two cases it already has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the seller was not truly forced, because a small sale was possible with effort. So we are unsure whether his larger sale shows real need, or whether he is like the seller of the poor field, whose chasing the money proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: made an effort, went to trouble

phrases.english: But if he wants to sell for one hundred

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אַשְׁכַּח, וְאִי טָרַח הֲוָה מַשְׁכַּח,
phrases.english: and does not find [a buyer], but if he had made an effort he would have found one,
and he did not make the effort and sells for two hundred,
and he goes in and goes out for the money,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי: כְּמוֹכֵר שָׂדֵהוּ מִפְּנֵי רָעָתָהּ דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: what [is the law]? Is he considered like one who sells his field because of its poor quality,
or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי בָּעֵי לְזַבּוֹנֵי בִּמְאָה וְלָא אַשְׁכַּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the obvious case to a harder, borderline case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a seller who could have avoided the larger sale with effort, yet chases his money, counts as selling from need or like the poor-field seller.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found. The question remains open.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says תיקו, which means it could not settle the question from step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source decides whether the 'didn't bother' seller is like the needy seller or like the poor-field seller. So the doubt is left standing.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand: the question is left unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: A seller who chases his money after being forced into a larger sale shows need, so the buyer does not acquire. If he could have avoided that sale with effort, the law is a תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand [unresolved].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 3 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The borderline case remains a doubt.

steps.title: The משנה: workers who back out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if one hired a donkey driver or a potter who then backed out, he may hire others at their expense, or trick them.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] If one hired the donkey driver and the potter, etc., he may hire [others] at their expense, or deceive them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה. This sets up a question about what that משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה protects an employer whose workers quit at a moment when his goods would be lost. He may pay new workers more and charge the first workers, or he may promise them extra pay to come back.

phrases.aramaic: שָׂכַר אֶת הַחַמָּר וְאֶת הַקַּדָּר וְכוּ׳
phrases.english: If one hired the donkey driver and the potter, etc.
he may hire [others] at their expense, or deceive them.
phrases.notes: 'Deceive' means he may promise them extra pay to finish the job and then not give it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the גמרא returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Workers who back out where there is a loss may be replaced at their expense, or tricked into returning.

steps.title: How much may he spend at their expense?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the limit is on hiring replacements at the first workers' expense.
steps.simpleTranslation: Up to how much may he hire at their expense?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the משנה: how much extra cost can be charged to the workers who quit?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not give a limit. The גמרא wants to know the exact amount the employer may charge.

phrases.english: Up to how much may he hire at their expense?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the limit on the ruling quoted in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The maximum amount the employer may charge the workers who backed out.

steps.title: רב נחמן: Up to their wages
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says he may spend only up to the wages he owes the first workers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Up to [the amount of] their wages.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question: the limit is the wages the first workers would have received.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The employer may use the money he owes the quitting workers to pay the replacements more. He cannot charge them beyond that amount.

keyTerms.meaning: up to the amount of their wages

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
Up to [the amount of] their wages.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: עַד כְּדֵי שְׂכָרָן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The limit is the wages owed to the original workers.

steps.title: רבא challenges: a ברייתא says up to 40 or 50 זוז
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects from a ברייתא that lets the employer spend up to 40 or 50 זוז, which is more than the workers' wages.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא raised an objection to רב נחמן: [It was taught:] up to forty or fifty זוז!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב נחמן with a ברייתא that seems to allow a much higher amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the employer may spend up to 40 or 50 זוז, the limit is not just the workers' wages. This seems to contradict רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: he raised an objection to him (from a ברייתא or משנה)

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection to Rav Naḥman:
Up to forty or fifty zuz!
phrases.notes: He is quoting a ברייתא about this same case of workers who back out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's limit from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that the limit is the workers' wages.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא allows a set sum of 40 or 50 זוז, which can be more than the wages, so wages cannot be the limit.

steps.title: The ברייתא is when the worker's bundle is in his hands
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the ברייתא is talking about a case where the worker's bundle of belongings came into the employer's possession.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: When that [ברייתא] was taught, it was where the bundle came into his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends himself by limiting the ברייתא to a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the employer holds the worker's bundle, he has something extra to collect from, so he may spend more. Without the bundle, he can only use the wages he owes, so רב נחמן's limit still stands.
steps.whatToRemember: An employer may charge workers who back out for replacements up to the wages he owes them. If he holds their bundle, he may charge more, up to 40 or 50 זוז.

phrases.english: He said to him: When that was taught,
it was where the bundle came into his hand.
phrases.notes: The worker's bundle ended up with the employer, so the employer has something extra to collect from.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction: the ברייתא is talking about a case where the employer holds the worker's bundle.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows 40 or 50 זוז in every case, which would contradict רב נחמן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Normally the limit is the wages. Only when the bundle is in the employer's hands may he spend more.

steps.title: Renter changed the donkey's route and it died
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a renter who took the donkey on a mountain instead of a valley, or the reverse, is liable if it dies, even when both routes are the same length.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone rents a donkey to take it on a mountain but takes it in a valley, or rents it for a valley but takes it on a mountain, he is liable if it dies. This is true even if both routes are ten מיל long.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says that if a renter changes the agreed route and the donkey dies, he must pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The distance is exactly the same, so he did not overwork the donkey by going farther. Even so, changing the kind of terrain counts as breaking the deal, and he is liable for the death.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין: 'our משנה'. It marks the start of a new משנה.
One who rents (here, the person renting the donkey)
A unit of distance, roughly a kilometer

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who rents a donkey to lead it on a mountain
and he led it in a valley,
or rented it for a valley and he led it on a mountain,
even if this route is ten mil
and that route is ten mil,
and it died, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַשּׂוֹכֵר אֶת הַחֲמוֹר לְהוֹלִיכוֹ בָּהָר וְהוֹלִיכוֹ בַּבִּקְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion about workers who back out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A renter who changes the donkey's route between mountain and valley is liable if it dies, even when the distance is equal.

steps.title: Slipping versus overheating depends on which route caused it
steps.stepSummary: The משנה separates two kinds of harm. Slipping is blamed on the mountain, and overheating is blamed on the valley. The renter pays only when the route he switched to caused the harm.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he rented the donkey for a mountain but took it in a valley: if it slipped, he is exempt; if it overheated, he is liable. If he rented it for a valley but took it on a mountain: if it slipped, he is liable; if it overheated, he is exempt. But if it overheated because of the climb, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives a more detailed rule. Whether the renter pays depends on whether the new route caused the specific injury.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slipping is a mountain danger, so it is not blamed on a valley route. Heat is a valley danger, so it is not blamed on a mountain route. The last line adds an exception: if the hard climb up the mountain caused the overheating, the mountain is to blame after all, and he is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt, does not have to pay

phrases.english: One who rents a donkey to lead it on a mountain
and he led it in a valley,
if it slipped, he is exempt,
but if it overheated, he is liable.
If he rented it to lead it in a valley and he led it on a mountain,
if it slipped, he is liable,
but if it overheated, he is exempt,
but if it overheated because of the ascent, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשּׂוֹכֵר אֶת הַחֲמוֹר לְהוֹלִיכָהּ בָּהָר וְהוֹלִיכָה בַּבִּקְעָה, אִם הֶחְלִיקָה – פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a second ruling that distinguishes between kinds of harm, unlike the first ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The renter is liable only when the harm is the kind typical of the route he switched to (slipping on a mountain, heat in a valley), or when the uphill climb caused the overheating.

steps.title: What the owner owes when the rented donkey becomes useless
steps.stepSummary: If the donkey becomes ill or is seized for government service, the owner can simply hand it over as is. If it dies or breaks a leg, the owner must provide another donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone rents a donkey and it becomes ill or is seized for government work, the owner says to him: 'Here is yours in front of you.' If it dies or breaks, the owner must provide him with a donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה switches to a new case. Now the question is what the owner owes the renter when the donkey becomes unusable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ill or seized donkey still exists and may recover or come back, so the owner can tell the renter to take it as it is. A dead or broken donkey is gone for this job, so the owner must replace it.

keyTerms.meaning: Forced labor: being seized by the government for public service
'Here is yours in front of you.' Take what you rented as it is.

steps.confusionAlert: In this case the one who may have to pay is the OWNER, not the renter. Steps 10 and 11 dealt with the renter's liability. Here the question is what the owner owes the renter.

phrases.english: One who rents a donkey and it became ill
or it was seized for public service,
the owner says to him: Here is yours in front of you.
If it died or it broke a leg,
the owner is obligated to provide him with a donkey.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, 'him', is added in the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשּׂוֹכֵר אֶת הַחֲמוֹר וְהִבְרִיקָה אוֹ שֶׁנַּעֲשֵׂית אַנְגַּרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a separate ruling in the same משנה about the owner's duty to the renter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Illness or seizure: the owner may hand over the donkey as it is. Death or breaking: the owner must provide a replacement donkey.

steps.title: Why does only the second ruling make distinctions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the first ruling makes the renter liable across the board, while the second ruling splits between slipping and overheating.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is different about the first part, which does not make a distinction, and what is different about the later part, which does make a distinction?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by asking about the משנה. It sets up the next steps, which will explain what kind of death the first ruling is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 says 'liable' with no conditions, while Step 11 sets conditions based on the cause. The גמרא wants to know what is special about the case in the first ruling that makes it impossible to split.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא. It marks the start of the discussion on the משנה.
'What is different?' Asks for the reason two cases are treated differently.
The first clause of a משנה
The later clause of a משנה
Makes a distinction, divides between cases

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא דְּלָא קָא מְפַלֵּיג,
phrases.english: What is different about the first clause, which does not distinguish,
and what is different about the latter clause, which does distinguish?
phrases.notes: The 'latter clause' here means the slipping and overheating ruling (Step 11).

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא דְּלָא קָא מְפַלֵּיג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by comparing the first two rulings of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case is the first ruling talking about, such that it does not divide by the cause of death the way the second ruling does?

steps.title: School of רבי ינאי: the donkey died from the air
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי says the first ruling is about a death caused by the air. Either place's air could have killed it, so no split by terrain is possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי said: The first part is where it died because of the air. We can say the mountain air killed it, and we can say the valley air killed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer explains the first ruling: it is about a donkey that died from the change in air.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slipping and heat each belong to one kind of terrain, so they can be split. Death from air could come from either kind, so the משנה cannot say which route is to blame. The renter who changed the route is therefore liable either way.

keyTerms.meaning: Scholars from the school (study hall) of רבי ינאי

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai said:
The first clause is where it died because of the air,
since we say the air of the mountain killed it,
and we say the air of the valley killed it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי: רֵישָׁא שֶׁמֵּתָה מֵחֲמַת אֲוִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13 by defining the cause of death in the first ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first ruling is about death from the air, which either terrain could cause, so it cannot be split and the renter is liable.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר חנינא: the donkey died from exhaustion
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא explains the first ruling differently: it is about a donkey that died from exhaustion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: It is a case where it died from exhaustion.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different answer to the same question about the first ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He also places the first ruling in a cause of death that is not tied to slipping or heat. So again the משנה cannot divide by terrain, and the renter who changed the route is liable.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said:
For example, where it died because of exhaustion.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁמֵּתָה מֵחֲמַת אוּבְצָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to Step 13, parallel to Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first ruling is about death from exhaustion.

steps.title: רבה: a snake bit the donkey
steps.stepSummary: רבה gives a third explanation: the first ruling is about a donkey that was bitten by a snake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: It is a case where a snake bit it.
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא answers the same question with yet another kind of death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A snake bite can happen on a mountain or in a valley, so it is not tied to one type of ground. That is why the first ruling cannot split, and the renter who changed the route is liable.
steps.whatToRemember: The first ruling (Step 10) has no conditions because it is about a cause of death that is not tied to one kind of terrain. Three opinions describe it: air (school of רבי ינאי), exhaustion (רבי יוסי בר חנינא), and a snake bite (רבה). In all three, the renter who changed the route is liable.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
For example, where a snake bit it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third answer to Step 13, alongside Steps 14 and 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first ruling is about a snake bite, which can happen on either kind of terrain.

steps.title: The first ruling follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא, quoting רבי יוחנן, says the first ruling of the משנה follows רבי מאיר. רבי מאיר holds that anyone who goes against the owner's intention gets a strict ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Whose opinion is this ruling? It is רבי מאיר's. He says that anyone who goes against what the owner wanted...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a fourth answer to the question from step 13. It explains the first ruling by naming the תנא behind it instead of describing a special type of death. The sentence is cut off here and finishes on the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answers in steps 14 to 16 kept the first ruling in line with the second ruling's split by pointing to a cause of death that is not tied to one kind of terrain: the air, exhaustion, or a snake bite. רבי יוחנן does something different. He says the first ruling comes from רבי מאיר, whose rule is that going against the owner's wishes makes a person fully responsible. On this reading, the renter is liable across the board because he changed the route, no matter how the donkey died.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this? This is a standard way to say which תנא a ruling follows.
One who goes against the intention or agreed terms of someone else.
The owner. Here it means the owner of the donkey, the one who rented it out.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not one more 'special kind of death' answer like the previous three. Instead of narrowing the case, it assigns the ruling to a specific תנא, רבי מאיר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common move in the גמרא: when two rulings in one משנה seem to clash, one way out is to say they come from different תנאים.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Whose opinion is this? It is Rabbi Meir's,
phrases.notes: "This" means the first ruling of the משנה, where the renter is liable no matter what.

phrases.english: who says: anyone who goes against the intention
of the owner,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a fourth answer to the question in step 13. The previous three answers each named a special cause of death; this one attributes the first ruling to רבי מאיר instead.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the first ruling make the renter liable across the board, while the second ruling splits between slipping and overheating?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first ruling follows רבי מאיר, who treats anyone who goes against the owner's intention strictly. So any change of route makes the renter liable for whatever happens to the donkey.
